utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I am informed that Mr. Piletta-Zanin would like to address the Chamber and I see that Mr. Ierace is on his feet. Since I've got no idea what it is about -- I wonder.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I am on my feet to address you, it is for technical reasons and I need to add that the Defence is not behaving "goody goody" as they say in English, but we are on our feet because of "goody" as that was mentioned yesterday. I am saying this because the witness will go back and perhaps we shall not be able to show what we wanted to show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let's try to cut it short. If you want to tell us that goody in your view was relating to the question rather than anything else I would like to invite Mr. Ierace to check the transcript very carefully and then see whether he could agree. I have clearly in my mind also the way in which it was said. He said, that's a goody. And he --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, indeed Mr. President and that is the case and that is why I am on my feet. I thought I would see it in the copy but I didn't see but nevertheless, we remember it. If that was the case, in view of this witness personality, one could admit that he wasn't wrong, that would be -- it would be a matter of courtesy of politeness to admit that he was not wrong. Secondly, what I wanted to say, we received from the Prosecution copies of the tape but after we received the black box and the grey box, the images are completely impossible to see it is completely illegible except for the first two segments, all the rest is completely useless. We simply cannot -- we cannot use them. We cannot work with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, it was my recollection that after the witness said "That's a goody," that he one line later said "That wasn't a good day." Therefore -- and it's understanding of the Chamber that the witness referred when he said, "That's a goody," to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it might have something to do with the vernacular of antillians. My interpretation of what the witness meant by those words in terms of their colloquial use is to paraphrase, this was an excellent example, a goody is an excellent example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps an excellent example of a very bad day because that's what he said one line later so whether he said it's good that you ask me or that is a good example, but your questions seem to indicate that that's a goody refers to a good event which it is at least not the interpretation of the Chamber. Would you please keep that in mind and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I might add that it was in the circumstances a little bizarre in terms of the choice of words by the witness, which is why I drew it to his attention and not surprisingly, he withdrew it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's -- it needs no further -- I mean if it was whatever it was, whether it was a comment on the question, I think the witness should refrain from commenting on whether the question is a good one or a bad one. I think the matter has been sufficiently clarified. If necessary, I'll come back to it. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this is -- we are talking about the way a witness is approached. I said I'll come back to it with the witness and -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am talking about what the Prosecution said. The Prosecution says why it was withdrawn but that is not true, the witness said, no I did not say that and if I did then I apologise and I withdraw it. His first reaction was I did not say that and one cannot interpret at this point in time the word used by a witness and I'd really like -- I'd appreciate it if Mr. Ierace would have this in mind and take note of what the witness says. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter has been sufficiently clarified by now by observation of the Chamber, response of Mr. Ierace and the observations by the Defence. Is there any other issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will turn into private session. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gray.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, how are you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gray, may I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony and Mr. Ierace will now resume the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Mr. Gray?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. How are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Good, thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To start, did you check your statement to see the date that you visited the school of theology in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did last night and I'm sorry I can't tell you the precise date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There's no reference in your statement to the school of theology, is there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness please make a break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us there was a written agreement between the warring parties that Lukavica barracks was not a legitimate target and you said that it was part of the heavy weapons agreement; do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you checked, not that I asked you, but have you checked the text of that agreement to see if that is correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I would like to note that in line -- page 8, line 8, I think is gone now, says David Gray and your name is Richard Paul, am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Your name is Richard Paul?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Not David. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be an error in the transcript. It is Mr. Richard Gray who testifies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During the first break, would you mind checking the text of those agreements to see if there is any reference, not now, and indeed, I think there are four agreements, there is the written agreement between the UN and the Bosnian Serb forces in relation to the airport, secondly in relation to heavy weapons. There is a written agreement with the Presidency forces in relation to the airport, and a separate agreement in relation to heavy weapons; is that correct, four altogether?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were -- I mean there were -- there were agreements between the airport agreement that was the very first agreement. The second agreement was for the concentration of heavy weapons and the support of the airport agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have copies of all four of those agreements that you can check during the first break?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, yesterday, I showed you a video and perhaps Mr. President for the benefit of the accused, we might reshow it now that there is a transcript. Might I just check if the interpreting booths have copies of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In that case, if the witness's monitor could be placed on the correct channel we could replay the clip from yesterday and as we do it this time, Mr. Gray, could you take particular note of the appearance on the video at any stage of General MacKenzie.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the booth indicates they have three tapes, they are unsure which tape to play at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The tape is the one which doesn't have any markings and it does not have any writing on its spine. It's a tape which consists of I think nine clips. I think each of the other two tapes has some rough writing on the spine. If the booth is unsure then perhaps I could quickly look at them and in the meantime move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, you are requested to assist the technicians or you can go into the booth and assist them in finding the right tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the meantime, in the meantime, could we benefit from this interval to ask for the Prosecution to give us a legible copy of their tape because we cannot use ours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Prosecution is not at this point --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We have French interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have French interpretation on channel 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President, I think we've now located it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. May the tape be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That can be stopped, thank you and perhaps the screen could be put back on transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The French booth, Mr. President, the last sentence wasn't translated, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean the name of the -- what Mr. Ierace said or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's just been translated now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- you are referring to line -- that can be stopped?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, to the French booth, all the text that we heard, the entire text wasn't translated there was a part that was omitting. This is why I intervened briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you said the last line, the last line I heard was the name of the interviewer, the BBC, that was the line and you really felt it necessary to interrupt for that instead of putting that on a piece of paper, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Then take five minutes to think over what the task is in this Court. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that when the second round of mortars, the second group fell, you were inside in the conference room, what was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. happening in the conference room?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were having a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise for talking over you. They were having a meeting, who was having a meeting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The foreign secretary and Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So you were in the meeting between them. Does that appear on the video at any stage?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They concentrated on the principal people in the actual meeting. I was sitting to one side out of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We saw what appeared to be a press conference, whereabouts did that take place?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The press conference I believe took place in the PTT.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing General MacKenzie on the tape during that conference?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing General MacKenzie on the tape following Sir Douglas Hurd's arrival at the airport?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you still have with you the excerpt of General MacKenzie's book that you looked at yesterday? Might it be shown to the witness, it's P3778.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, I saw that you have a copy yourself as well but with some markings on it -- we see yellow markings, we'd prefer you use the copy given to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you need to consult your own markings then please ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you place those yellow markings on your copy overnight?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do I take it that you read it very carefully after court last night?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice when you read it that General MacKenzie said in his published account, that he didn't go to the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recall yesterday you told us a number of times that General MacKenzie accompanied Sir Douglas Hurd to the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my recollection at the time, but having read the account, and having seen the videotape again, General MacKenzie normally travelled in a VBL which is a small --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll stop you there, Mr. Gray. You did tell us a number of times yesterday, didn't you, that General MacKenzie accompanied Sir Douglas Hurd to the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, when you told us that, you sincerely believed it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We spoke about the pandemonium which, on your account, followed the two mortar shells that landed immediately before Sir Douglas Hurd and General MacKenzie arrived at the Presidency and how Sir Douglas Hurd was shepherded or moved through that pandemonium into the Presidency; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the video, we see two injured people following the mortar attack and we hear Martin Bell say that there were five injured as a result of the attack. He doesn't mention any people killed, does he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And we don't see any people killed, do we?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, but I can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... might not reflect what is in view of you to be seen on the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, but what I can say is that death is not always immediate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question was whether any people killed were to be seen on the video. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. The objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We don't see any people killed on the video, do we?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you actually do, but they may be shown as being wounded but the man that was lying on the ground was -- he was basically dead. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see. The two -- all right. Do you remember yesterday that you told us that there were people who were killed on the spot?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And if that happened, it is odd that Martin Bell didn't say as much, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The media put their own interpretation on many events that happened in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, Martin Bell was a very experienced war correspondent, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was and you can see where he gets wounded on one of the videotapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Are you telling us that he was prejudiced?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that as a media person, he put his own interpretation on many things that he saw like many, many other media people who were in Sarajevo and if you want to go through all the tapes, I will tell you what is actually the facts and what is the interpretation placed by the media on events and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir if you could stop for a minute, please. This isn't a matter of interpretation. Your intimating that Martin Bell deliberately did not report that people were killed at the Presidency, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yeah. Other BBC journalists included Kate Adie who was in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did she take up duties after Martin Bell himself fell victim to a shelling?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a number of BBC journalists who were in Sarajevo at the time, but I believe that Kate Adie -- it was probably yes. I mean I wasn't following who was reporting on things. I mean but I believe Kate Adie was one of the people that took up the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, have you read Martin Bell's book on his time in Sarajevo entitled "In harm's way"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the video, we saw the procession of APCs downtown to the Presidency; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that, indeed a number of times, that when a dignitary who arrived in Sarajevo, the UN was very careful to not disclose that dignitary's programme with one side to the other side; do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were intimating that the Bosnian Serb side were not informed by the UN as to where Sir Douglas Hurd would be travelling in Sarajevo and certainly not informed as to the time that he would be arriving at the Presidency, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were intimating that therefore, the Bosnian Serbs, their forces could not be responsible for the mortaring, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serbs, I take it, were informed that Sir Douglas Hurd would be in Sarajevo that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were they given a time and place for their people to meet up with Sir Douglas Hurd?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember now what time that was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, but they met up, I'm fairly certain, at the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mean before or after he went to the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you wouldn't have to be a genius to deduce that following that meeting, Sir Douglas Hurd was likely to meet the president and that that meeting would probably take place, as others did, at the Presidency; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree but some meetings actually took place at the PTT.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And in order to work out where the meeting was to take place, from the hills surrounding Sarajevo, one only had to observe the procession of UN vehicles, didn't one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could have done that, but I mean I was in UN vehicles as well, I mean and I preceded Douglas Hurd.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Gray, with the greatest of respect, what difference does that make?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that if you look at the landscape of Sarajevo, and you look at the visibility of what you can see from the surrounding Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. countryside looking down into Sarajevo, you could see that I went in an APC to the Presidency --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We don't have a lot of time, Mr. Gray, let me stop you --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Douglas Hurd was delayed in his arrival at the Presidency and that is quite clearly shown in the excerpt that you've given us, and so yes, there was a convoy of APCs but I go back to my primary point about this whole incident which is that I was standing at the very front door of the Presidency and I heard the primary --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll come to that, Mr. Gray, please stop. You don't dispute, do you, that the procession could be seen from the hills?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably could be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Stop. Now, did it occur to you that the Bosnian Serb forces most probably had individuals in the city who were able to communicate with them and relay their observations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that you never saw someone who identified himself as being part of the Bosnian Serb forces holding a walkie-talkie communicating with forces in the hills; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You never saw it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No. But as an experienced military officer, you would presume it, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you not think that was an obvious intelligence move for the Bosnian Serb forces to take?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's not my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to slow down not only for the interpreters but also for the court reporters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, you said that there was some more footage on this incident, a brown Mercedes, is that footage which shows a brown Mercedes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure that the witness said that there were other incidents but there were other photographs that concerned this incident as far as I can remember. The witness said we could see the scene from another perspective but he didn't mention an incident itself, the incident itself, not as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not see in the English text the word incident -- yes, could you please in the English text refer to where I find the incident mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it was in the closing stages of last night's evidence when the witness said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I was -- I was looking to your question and my question was to Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Yes, or is it not completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean Mr. Ierace's question? My question had to do with the term "in this incident," I don't think the witness said that there was any reports about this incident but he spoke about the site of the incident as far as I can remember so if Mr. Ierace could be more precise, I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes, if you would then please continue, Mr. Ierace. If, however, there is a clear -- I have to check that in the transcript, but please inform us, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I can save some time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember mentioning a brown Mercedes last night?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And basically you told us there was some footage somewhere on those tapes of a brown Mercedes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And that was footage taken in relation to this incident outside the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When Sir Douglas Hurd attended?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now to help me identify that footage, as you remember it, do we see a brown Mercedes on the road, a door open, shrapnel splattered and then a close up of a mortar impact on the ground?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've got it. You've got the one. That's it. That is the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We've got to pause between our exchanges?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the video booth has that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. excerpt frozen on a tape --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, before doing so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the witness yesterday said, yes there is. It shows a brown Mercedes car. Okay. And it's immediately when the two first mortar bombs landed it was taken directly from the Presidency side of I mean the tape you've shown was coming from the PTT side. That is therefore the same incident. May I remind you that yesterday, you interrupted Mr. Ierace on something that had hardly any -- hardly any impact that is whether one or two ambulances were there. The issue was whether they were there at the specific moment. You nevertheless felt it necessary to object because the witness had been saying that there was one ambulance instead of ambulances. You did not check the transcript well because two lines after he talked about one ambulance, he talked about ambulances in the plural. Now, again, you interrupt without having properly done your homework. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, objecting is a full right. This right should be used in a diligent way. That's where the right has been given for. Now again, it's clearly from the testimony of the witness yesterday that it was the same incident. I would like you to take another five minutes to do the same as I invited to you before. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, I think you said, correct me if I am wrong, this is the footage, is it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the brown Mercedes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the Witness's screen might be adjusted so he can see the relevant image. Do you see on your screen a brown Mercedes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see me, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you see yourself in the picture at the moment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We can't see where you point to so don't try pointing to the screen. Can you describe to us where you appear in this image?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the one. That's it. How do I point?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see what appears to be a bus shelter on the left side?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Presidency is over on the right-hand side of this Mercedes and you can see the splatter mark where --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Keep in mind that when you point to the screen, we can't see you we can't see where you point so you have to use words to describe where you are. As we look down the road beyond the roof of the Mercedes, are you saying the Presidency is --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please wait until I finish my questions so the interpreters don't get pressured too much. All right. And I think we can see towards the -- just beyond the back windscreen of the Mercedes the rear view windscreen some individuals by the road, are you one of those?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I am not. I'm standing on the actual steps of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think in the distance we can see a light post with a white vehicle perhaps at the base of a light post, do you mean somewhere around there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is to the right of the picture is where the Presidency is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You can't recognise yourself in this picture, can you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry I thought you earlier said that you were?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, first of all, would you agree with me that the segment of news in which this image appears on your tape is a BBC segment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And like all of the 60 or so others, somewhere around two or three minutes long? Each of the segments is about two or three minutes long; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. The news report in which this footage appears, according to the voice, the commentary, makes no reference to the Presidency, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to review the actual clip myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. In that case, we'll line it up and show it to you after the break and I'll move on to something else?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mentioned to us the other day a shelling of a market; do you remember doing that? You said that you sent an artillery officer and a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. mortar officer down to investigate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked about the bombing of a market. I didn't talk about the shelling of a market.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I stand corrected. I think you said that market was within walking distance of the PTT; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've actually walked past it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you told us you did not recall the date; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And would you be able to indicate the position if you were shown the map that you marked the other day?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I probably would. I would give you the approximate area of where it was but I went shopping one day to try and get some food and I walked past the area where the marketplace was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, please wait?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you keep your answers short, I'd greatly appreciate it and you're telling us that you probably could indicate the position so I ask that the witness be shown the map which is Exhibit D1845. Would you please take a blue pen and place a cross to indicate the position of the market. If you don't know the exact position then circle the area within which, to the best of your recollection, the market was located.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, just to be clear about this, we're not talking about what became known as the bread line shelling in Sarajevo in 1992, are we?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We are?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember on the clip that we saw on the visit of Douglas Hurd we saw that he -- I withdraw that. We saw that on the day of his visit, there was a ceremony carried out by musicians likely and internationally known as Adagio day. Do you recall seeing that on the clip?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And we saw I think a famous cellist playing at the site of a massacre, an alleged massacre are you saying that that incident is the same one that you sent the artillery officer and the mortar officer down to carry out an inspection?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No. To the best of your recollection -- go on?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That cellist appears a number of times on the tapes as I'm sure you realise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I mean it's not just once that he appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, that's right. What do you remember of the events that were taking place as you heard them, the events that took place immediately before this shelling as they were related to you from whatever source?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the events that happened immediately before it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes before the incident which took place --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the marketplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Within the circle that you have marked on the map, this incident?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was absolutely totally quiet, there was no shelling, no machine-gun fire, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was it a crowded market, a market that wasn't well attended on this particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was crowded, people wanted to get food.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there items on the food stalls, on the stalls?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And do you remember what time of day it was --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the middle -- it was middle of the day and there was actually footage of the actual bombing on the videotapes that I've provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How long was it -- I withdraw that. Do you remember what day of the week it was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember where you were when you were first told about it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was probably in the PTT or I was in a meeting in Lukavica barracks. I could have been in the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The answer therefore is no, I don't remember?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember how long it was after you heard about it that you dispatched and artillery officer and a mortar officer to visit the scene?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did it as soon as I got back to the PTT. I think I -- I think from memory, I think I was actually at Lukavica barracks having a meeting with the Serbs about the concentration of weapons and when I returned to the PTT, I heard about the bombing in the market and I immediately dispatched the Australian major artillery to that location and the Canadian captain mortar officer to that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you instruct them to carry out an analysis of whatever markings and remains there were at the scene?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that they informed you that they found no evidence of a mortaring or shelling, no tail fins; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you seriously expect that by the time they got there, the tail fins would be lying around?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I mean the -- from the last, the last video clip that you actually showed, okay, you can see on the ground the clear markings of what a mortar bomb does and there were no such markings and there were no such markings for an artillery shell and I previously explained this to the Court that an artillery shell will leave a specific marking on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My question was about tail fins, Mr. Gray, if you could please focus on the question. But in relation to markings on the ground, did you arrange for any witnesses or surviving victims to be interviewed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiries as to whether the Bosnian government authorities had carried out an investigation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. It was not my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How could it be your job to carry out a UN investigation and yet not arrange for eyewitnesses to be interviewed or to read -- to access a copy of the government investigation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a specific task in Sarajevo and that was as the senior military observer for the observers in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many shells were said to have landed, how many explosions were said to have taken place?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given that witnesses were not spoken to, other investigations, the fruits of other investigations were not checked, how can you exclude the possibility that the mortar shell landed on a person?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mortar shell landing on a person is a one in a million chance, it's like winning lotto or losing lotto, yeah, so I mean it is -- it is just so remote, it just doesn't even bear thinking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't know that you ever really explained to us the situation in relation to tail fins. Did you not allow for the possibility that if there was a tail fin, that it would have been taken by the time the officers got there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact of the matter, and I would really like to leave this alone, the fact of the matter is that I sent two very experienced officers, one Australian, one Canadian. They went to the marketplace. They clearly examined every inch of it and there was no indication of any impact from an artillery shell or a mortar shell. There was one crater which was clearly from a bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see. So the crater was actually clearly from a bomb?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see. How do you know they looked at the right crater if they didn't speak to any witnesses?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, at that stage, Sarajevo was peppered with impact?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, give me a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Explosions, impact markings, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, but in the marketplace, there was nothing else apart from tables umbrellas, okay, to actually cover the food, and so on, and there was one crater there. That's all. There were no other mortar bomb markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, Mr. Gray, did I hear you say very softly, "Give me a break"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You should understand that both parties are entitled to ask further questions on the issues you are testifying about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no need to get nervous about that even if Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you think that the Prosecution does not understand your answers clearly. By answering the following questions, you will have an opportunity to tell exactly what your recollection of these events is. If you need a break now, please tell me or if you say no, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please keep in mind these questions are part of a trial and not an attack on you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We'll come back to the video for that, Mr. Gray, at a later point when it's lined up. Now, you were shown some video by the Defence of a convoy of white vehicles approaching Sarajevo and let me remind you what you said about it, "They were a resupply convoy that had come in from Belgrade and they were ambushed by the Muslims." And then later, "There were about 20 lorries in it and a point, a very serious point about this whole ambush was that it was totally deliberate, that the Presidency forces knew that this convoy was coming through and they even had a video camera team there to actually film the ambush on these French."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: "I've already given evidence to the UN arm about this particular ambush. I did that in 1992."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And then you were asked, "Colonel, can you think of a reason or do you know the reason for which this convoy was attacked?" Answer: "I have no idea and I have no idea why I was personally attacked 13 times." Now, I'd ask the booth if we can play the other of the two tapes I looked at earlier, it just has one segment on it and it's P3794. I think the transcript is about to be distributed. Here is the transcript. And if we could just hold off playing it until all have the transcript. Just hold it. Thank you. Yes, please play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A very different account, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A very different account?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From the tape, from what you have told us. Not an ambush but in part incompetence they drove straight into a battle that had been going for three days. It's a different account, that's my first point, Mr. Gray?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. Second point -- first of all, the voice is that of Kate Adie, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: She indicates from that report that it was made the day following the incident, she refers to the incident taking place "at dusk yesterday," do you accept that that's when she filed her report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And she said, "According to the soldiers, they drove into the fight," indicating that she spoke to the French soldiers for her information.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: She may have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So it seems your account on the strength of that tape is at odds with the account of the French soldiers whose comrades were killed and wounded; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my account is. May I give my account?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, you may?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I do that now?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you would like to tell us what evidence there was from your perspective that it was an ambush rather than a three-day battle that was inadvertently driven into?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I actually arranged for a cease-fire with the warring parties. You can see from the video pictures, I mean, it was a arranged for a specific time for that convoy to actually come through. You can see from the pictures that it was broad daylight and the convoy was deliberately targeted, I mean, it was clearly identifiable as a UN convoy and I had spoken to the liaison officers in the PTT prior to that convoy coming through and it was deliberately targeted. It was ambushed and it was fired at from the Presidency side and they had a video camera crew or -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll stop you there, you've told us about that. Now, it was not unusual for journalists, for the UN to be fired at when they drove in the vicinity of the airport, was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. They could be fired at from both sides?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could be, but they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: According to you, that's true. The UN did not command much respect in the eyes of the civilians in Sarajevo, did it, at that stage?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want to read this?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Listen to the questions, please. You -- I take it in your answer, are conceding that there was a battle that had been going on. Had it been going on for three days at that point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battle had been continuous and you really have to take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You really must take a grain of salt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that the witness was strictly in agreement with the question which was asked of him and that is whether they didn't the journalist say this and that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is not an objection to a question as far as I can see and it's a comment on the consistency between question and answer. It is not up to counsel to comment on the consistency during cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Up until the arrival of the UN convoy -- I withdraw that. Had there been a particular intensity of the fighting in that area earlier that day and the previous day and the day before that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The time of the arrival of that particular convoy was unfortunate because there had been a lot of fighting, I mean they were driving down --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Gray, listen to the question. You say that the timing was unfortunate because there had been a lot of fighting and you've told us that you negotiated a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You wouldn't have done that unless you thought that was necessary, having regard to the level of fighting, I take it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many cease-fires I negotiated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's not the question, Mr. Gray. On this particular occasion, you thought it important to negotiate a cease-fire to ensure the safety of the convoy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, was that why you gave evidence because you were the one who negotiated the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, but it was also with regard to the presence of a video camera crew who were actually present at the actual time that the ambush took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And where were they from or --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were from Butmir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ask them where they were from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were from Butmir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please answer --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have to ask them anything. I didn't go down to the ambush site. I was busy doing something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, Mr. Ierace tried to further explore how you would know that they came from Butmir and that's what he asked you by saying, "Did you ask them?" Then you said, "I didn't have to ask them anything." I would like you to answer the question if you asked them, please say yes. If you didn't ask them as I take it from your answer, say no and then the next question will be put to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did anyone, to your knowledge, speak to this video crew and ask them where they came from, who they represented, why they were there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The French did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The French soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And we know what their view was, don't we, from the videotape?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, in your mind, you learned there was a video crew present and you joined the dots and concluded not only was it an ambush but the Bosnian authorities had the temerity to film the ambush; correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To use your words, the Muslims, the Muslims were at it again; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True and I can give you another example.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would that be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll adjourn until 11.00. --- Break taken at 10.27 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I received a request for a meeting in Chambers by one of the parties, a meeting that would take place in the presence of both parties. What I know what would be the subject it would certainly be a brief meeting and it could take place this afternoon at 2.30. So then I'll hear whether -- and I take it that if the party who requested it will inform the other party what it is about then I am willing to assist the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. At this stage I don't know anything about the subject matter but might we also be informed of the identity and sequence of witnesses for next week. I would be grateful if we could be told at least at this stage the name of the first witness for next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that this information will be given to you by the next break unless there's any reason that it cannot be done then I'd like to hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we can make a schedule that helps us too but I can tell you that on Monday, providing that we finish with Mr. Gray today, on Monday, our witness will be Mr. Vilicic who will be told by Mr. Kuljic and then by Mr. Terzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Mr. Usher could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, during the break did you check the text of the four documents that we mentioned earlier for any reference to Lukavica headquarters no longer being a legitimate target?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did you find any reference to that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, but the fact is that if you look at the original map for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters beg for a break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, may I ask you to look at your screen and to stop and wait until the text stops moving and then only then start to give your answer and Mr. Ierace will certainly look at his screen as well in order to follow the same procedure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you now agree that there was no written agreement between the parties which specified that Lukavica headquarters was not a legitimate target?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an agreement between the parties to not target Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Written?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is part of the -- I mean it's part of this map here that I have right here and Lukavica is right here and that was one of the concentration points and it was not supposed to be a target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A simple question, Mr. Gray, there was no written agreement, was there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we'll now see some video again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, you're about to see a video of the whole incident where the Mercedes footage is shown. Could we please see the Mercedes component.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: What exhibit number is that, Mr. Ierace, please for the record?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: 3798. At this stage, it hasn't been transposed on to a separate tape, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it may be played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am under the impression that this serves absolutely no purpose, there's no purpose in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Defence trying to assist people yet again, we don't have a translation into B/C/S and we don't have any translation into French. I won't say anything anymore because when I intervene, when I speak, I'm not supposed to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President there is not a transcript for that segment. It only became relevant during cross-examination in this morning's session. I think I can formulate my questions in relation to it in a way which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we need the text for your questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could do two things to replay the tape without text since the text, as Mr. Ierace tells us, is of no importance. We'll closely look at it that no question will be put to the witness at this moment for which any clue for an answer could be found in the text that has been pronounced by the reporter. Apart from that Mr. Ierace, the Prosecution is ordered in order to give General Galic an opportunity to at least know what has been said to provide for a transcript as soon as possible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please replay the tape without sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace before you put the questions to the witness. The Chamber would have preferred if you would have informed the Chamber either way that there was no transcript so that we could have considered to play the video footage without sound right away. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I accept I should have done that, Mr. President, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Going on the images, this appears to be one of the BBC reports by Martin Bell as to events in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There was no footage which appeared to relate to the visit of Sir Douglas Hurd; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you accept that the Mercedes that we saw in a shelled condition was not an incident which occurred during the visit of Sir Douglas Hurd?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not, it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, earlier you waved a document around, earlier this morning and said something to the effect that it was evidence or proof of your theories about the Bosnian Muslims. Would you please pass that document to the Court orderly so that I can see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it just had to do with the fact that the witness might not know which document is concerned but since he's taking his time to find it, everything is all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, whilst the witness is doing that in order to save time, I hand up a document that I'll shortly be showing to the witness P3797. Refrain from showing it to the witness at this stage but if it could be shown to the Defence and the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Gray, I think you've handed me a letter dated the 8th of September addressed from you to someone indicated as DPR 1, who was DPR 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President. To avoid any confusion, I think that there are several documents that were provided -- that were given to Mr. Ierace by the witness. We should know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will come to that, one document at a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who was DPR 1?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deputy permanent representative for the New Zealand permanent mission to the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. There are some documents attached to the letter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One appears to be an article from --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I object. I object. Mr. President, we haven't had the opportunity of seeing these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which have been provided like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the document, where does it come from and it is known to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, one of the documents, that is the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. letter and attachments was a document disclosed to the Prosecution by the Defence before this witness commenced his evidence. The other document, I'm unable to say at this stage whether it's been disclosed to us or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there more than one document that was addressed to DPR, as far as I understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm just going through that it appears to be a letter containing a number of annexes which was forwarded to that person, on the face of it, that's what it appears to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this sufficient to identify the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, I can't know off the top of my head what this is given that there are 50.000 documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And perhaps whilst the Defence looks at that document I can move on to another topic to save some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I asked the witness be shown 3797.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can't examine documents and focus on the questions. That's my position. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that one of the members of the team. We'll take a break of 30 seconds so in order to give you an opportunity to identify what document it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as we don't have all these documents with us for obvious reasons, I think that if we're going to ask about this document, it should be placed on the ELMO so that everyone can see it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When it comes to the content, perhaps the introductory questions could be without but then certainly the parties and the Bench should be able to follow the line of questioning. Could it please be returned to the Prosecution, the document. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that I circulate a document not to be shown to the witness at this page, P3787 and perhaps the earlier document P3797 might be withdrawn from the witness' table if it hasn't already been given -- if it has already been given to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was not yet given to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gray this is a letter that you sent with a number of attachments and the objective of the letter was to inform the recipient of material which established that the objective of the Bosnian government was to impose an Islamic regime; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It was also material to indicate that there was animosity on the part of Bosnian civilians towards the UN; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you please turn to the last page of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it please then be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The last page of the last annex, may that be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you've -- where is that document at this moment? Have you got the only one in your hands?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, this last document is an interview of the chief of the Yugoslav armed forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in on, I take it, the yellow marked part -- not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Carried out by the editor of an American magazine titled "Defence and foreign affairs strategic policy" being the journal for the 31st of December, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And it's the type of interview that back home we might call a Dorothy Dixer - D-I-X-E-R - would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've no idea what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that it's a type of interview where the questions are not challenging. The person being interviewed was hardly grilled, was he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No. Now, on that page, could we zoom into on the first column, the second last paragraph and we see reference to a U.S. Congressional report, I'll read the question. "The same U.S. Congressional report contains evidence of Mr. Izetbegovic's ties with fundamentalist Iran" and it says that "Mr. Izetbegovic made a deal with Tehran which before any escalation of conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina starts it is imperative Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that the sympathy of the west is won. For that reason, the Muslim special forces had carried out terror actions against their own people." Then the interviewer asks: "Is the JNA familiar with such acts?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And there were earlier references to this U.S. Congressional report; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take your word for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well have you read the article?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't had a chance to read the whole article.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, no, no, did you read it before you forwarded it on with your letter in 1993?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And this was one of the documents that you were waving around this morning, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The most important part about it is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you could just answer the question, Mr. Gray, rather than adding material. Might the witness be shown P3787. I'd like to show you another article published by a magazine called "Washington report on middle east affairs," July/August, 1993. If you would read to yourself the first paragraph. Do you accept that we have here a reference to that very same report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you know that four members of the congressional task force resigned in protest when this article was published?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please look at the last paragraph on the first page. I'll read out some pieces of it, "Although the document contains numerous quotes, none are footnoted and many are not even attributed. Most of the allegations" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the text be put on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher could you put the last paragraph of the first of the cover page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, if I could paraphrase this, it says most of the allegations levelled against Bosnian, Iran and various Muslim populations are derived from a very limited range of material, which support -- while support for the report's highly unorthodox reading of the shariah or Islamic law is based on a selective interpretation of the Koran and non-Islamic cultural practices within Muslim societies. It points out the word "terrorist" appears 27 times in the 14-page report and the authors, Forrest and Bodansky released it without consulting with the group's congressional members. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You go to the third page, second paragraph, we see a response from Alija Izetbegovic's personal representative in Washington, it is garbage, it is dirty lies he told the Washington report, it is based on fiction not fact. Then the next paragraph to finish off that paragraph, the representative said, any honest and knowledgeable congressman will immediately separate himself from this report, he said. And then this review goes on to say, four congressional members of the task force have done exactly that since last September, resigning from the organisation as a result of Forrest and Bodansky's report; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might that be returned and might the witness -- while the document is still in front of you, in relation to the article in Oslobodneje, can you understand why Sarajevans would have not been particularly impressed with the UN in mid-1992?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was extremely unfortunate the actual naming of the UN force and that was named the United Nations protection force which was extremely unfortunate because --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please stop. Understand that I appreciate the UN had a very difficult, if not impossible job in mid-1992 in Sarajevo and by the same token, if one places one's self in the shoes of Sarajevo civilians facing their first winter in that conflict, I suggest to you one can readily understand their dismay and shock, their disappointment at the attitude of the rest of the world to their plight as symbolised in the UN, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the dismay that they felt, the plight that they felt and their frustration but I have no excuse for them shooting at us and attacking us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you saw it. Now this article expresses that dismay in UNPROFOR, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It points out basically the general thrust of it is that the UN had it easy in Sarajevo compared to them, doesn't it? I'm not suggesting that you had it easy, don't misunderstand me, I'm suggesting this is the tenure, this is the tone of this article?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PAUL GRAY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since this line of questioning about the perceptions that the citizens of Sarajevo had from somewhere of the United Nations has nothing to do with these proceedings and I therefore object to the question and its relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.
